issues: After an out-of-range save fails (e.g. HR 999 -> vitals-state=failed, red error), typing a corrected value that happens to equal the last-saved value (e.g. back to 72) leaves vitals-state stuck at 'failed' with the stale error message, because the client diff vs saved.current is empty and no new PATCH is issued. Suggest: when onBlur/debounce produces an empty patch and current form equals saved snapshot across all keys, reset state back to 'saved' (or 'idle') and clear err. Low priority (DB is still correct).

action_items: Optional UX: VitalsPanel.save() should clear the 'failed' state + err when the resulting patch is empty (user typed a value equal to the last-persisted one).
critical_code_review_comments: VitalsPanel.save(): when patch is empty (user restored the last-saved value after a failed save) the function returns early without resetting state/err, so 'Save failed' + red error persist indefinitely. Add `if (!Object.keys(patch).length) { setState('saved'); setErr(''); return; }` or similar.

backend visit_save_vitals accepts raw dict without a Pydantic model; relies on validate_vitals + unknown-field check. Works correctly today but a dedicated BaseModel with Optional[float|int] fields would make OpenAPI contract explicit and keep validation co-located.
